rationale: Rodent infusion and isolated oil studies report coordination, exploratory movement or inconclusive rotarod performance. The isolated thymol aging model reports endurance, grip and rotarod differences. These do not establish fresh oregano exposure or a stride-length contrast in Parkinson disease.

Parkinson interviews and controlled whole-rhizome comparisons support a minimal favorable lean. The fresh-drink and exercise-versus-tea reports give conflicting pain data. The separate tea study reports favorable post-dose ratings with unknown root processing, and the survey has ambiguous ingredient labels. Capsule results are mixed. Preparation, diagnosis and pain differences limit the lean for grated ginger.
